newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P affirms Storebrand, Christiania Bank ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Storebrand, Christiania Bank ratings.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's (S&P) on Thursday affirmed the ratings of Norwegian insurer Storebrand and Christiania Bank that anounced plans to merge on Wednesday. The agency said the affirmations "reflect the potentially good strategic fit of the two groups".
Storebrand currently has A+ issuer credit and claims paying ability ratings.
Christiania Bank has A-2 commercial paper and short-term counterparty ratings.

S&P said the merger could create a dominant financial services group within Norway that would benefit from significant distribution advantages and diverse sources of revenue through strong franchises in life and non-life insurance markets and the banking sector.
"S&P considers the potential for the cross-selling of insurance and banking products to be significant," the agency said in a statement.
